# s2kt7_seed5 — regenerated s2kt7 data (base seed 5), LEAK-FIXED

Same regeneration as `../s2kt7_seed1` (fixes the seed-0 degeneracy where every click
dropped food at (0,0); see `../s2kt7/` and memory seed0-degenerate-data-gen), with
**base seed 5**. Generated by `../../scripts/gen_s2kt7_seed1.py --base-seed 5`.

Per-episode interpreter seeds (base 5 + disjoint per-split offsets): train 105-112,
test 305-306, test50 505-512. 8 / 2 / 8 episodes, 14 steps each, whitelist `noop,click`.
Real foraging: clicks spawn 2 food at random cells; ants step toward nearest food and eat.
Episodes are full trajectories (K-step context inline). See dynamics.txt for true mechanics.

## Test-leak fix (2026-08-10)

The ORIGINAL seed5 data (now preserved at `../s2kt7_seed5_leaky`) had a train→test50
action-sequence leak: `episode_actions` keyed the click-action plan off the episode
INDEX, so `train/episode_i` and `test50/episode_i` shared the IDENTICAL click sequence
(same locations, same order). Because click location is dynamics-irrelevant in s2kt7
(food spawns via `randomPositions`, ignoring click coords), the only thing distinguishing
clicks is their location label — and that shared sequence let a K=9-window decoder recover
exact test50 click locations by memorizing position-in-sequence, not by inverse dynamics
(memory s2kt7-seed5-run-and-leak).

The generator now keys `episode_actions` off the split-DISJOINT interpreter seed, so
train and test50 get DIFFERENT click sequences (verified: all 8 episode pairs differ).
The exact-location ID number is now honest (no leaked sequence to memorize); the real
learnable signal is click-vs-noop ("new food appeared ⇒ click, else noop").
